intro.line: One bottle of Hill Estate cold brew, delivered in Koramangala at 7:22 am.
intro.sub: Scroll to rewind seven months. A chief of staff did the work. People stepped in 8 times.

stages.line: Delivered at 7:22 am. At 8:20 am, sent his care note: fridge, ten days, one part to three parts milk.

running: Sending the care note to SI-30562
Scheduling a refill offer for day 8
managing: Pooja: asked for the refill nudge

chat.text: Care note sent to SI-30562, Koramangala. Keep it in the fridge, finish within ten days, 1 part to 3 parts milk.
Can he get a refill nudge before he runs out?
Set for day 8. At one glass a day, 30 ml each, 250 ml lasts about eight days.

stages.line: Chose Shadowfax for 560034: 1.4% late, the lowest of three couriers. Booked a 7 to 9 am drop so it arrives cold.

monitoring: Late rate by pincode, every 15 min

chat.text: Shadowfax picked up 54 parcels at 3:30 pm. His is on the 7 to 9 am drop: 1.4% late in 560034, lowest of three. Tracking sent.
Morning works. Thanks.

stages.line: Sent his order out of the cold room last, added an ice pack, and matched the weight to the kit: 640 g.

managing: Waiting on Farhan: 12 boxes to scan

card.ask: SI-30562 weighs 640 g packed with ice. The kit spec is 640 g.

chat.text: Cold-room batch is out. SI-30562 goes last so it leaves coldest. 640 g with the ice pack, matches the kit.
Scanned.
Ice packs in all 54. SI-30565 came in 120 g light, ice pack re-added. Van at 3:30 pm.

stages.line: Checked his order at 10:48 pm: address matches 560034. Booked it into the 8 am cold-room batch.

running: Booking SI-30562 into the 8 am batch
Queuing labels for the 8 am batch

chat.text: SI-30562 in from the dilution chat: Hill Estate, ₹449 prepaid. Address matches 560034. Booked into the 8 am cold-room batch.
Seen. Printing the batch now.

stages.line: At 10:37 pm he asked if it was too strong with milk. Answered in 2 minutes from the Hill Estate brew notes.
stages.ask: is this too strong if i add milk?
stages.answer: It's a concentrate, so cut it. 1 part to 3 parts cold milk tastes like a strong latte. Lighter: 1 to 4.

running: Pulling the Hill Estate brew notes
monitoring: Chats that turn into orders, daily

chat.text: is this too strong if i add milk?
It's a concentrate, so cut it. 1 part to 3 parts cold milk tastes like a strong latte. Lighter: 1 to 4.
ok perfect, ordering one

metrics.label: Dilution chats that end in an order

stages.line: 11 of 26 reviews asked how to dilute. Drafted a ratio-first line and tested two hero photos on 4,200 visits.

running: Switching the hero to the pour
Holding the new first line for Pooja
managing: Waiting on Pooja: 1 line to approve

decision.ask: Approve the new first line: "One part to three parts milk. A strong latte."
decision.signal: 11 of 26 reviews ask how to dilute

chat.text: 11 of 26 reviews ask how much to dilute. Drafted a new first line that leads with the 1 to 3 ratio.
Photo test done, 2,100 visits each. Pour over ice converts at 3.0%, bottle on white at 2.2%. Switched to the pour.
Reading it now.

os.title: Product page changes
rows: Estate cold brew, ready in minutes
One part to three parts milk. A strong latte.

stages.line: Cut three ads from the shoot. At 12:50 am, raised cut B, the pour, to ₹4,000 a day and paused cut C.

running: Raising cut B to ₹4,000 a day
Checking spend against the daily cap
managing: Waiting on Pooja: 1 cut to pick

card.ask: Pick the cut to scale this week. Cut B leads at ROAS 2.4.
card.signal: Cut B at ROAS 2.4, cut C at 0.8

chat.text: Cut B, the slow pour, is at ROAS 2.4. Raised it to ₹4,000 a day and paused cut C at 0.8.
B is the pour over ice?
Yes. Your pick sets it for the week.

stages.line: Wrote the brief and a ten-shot list with the slow pour as shot 4, held the studio, and sent call times.

running: Ordering 20 kg of ice for Thursday
managing: Waiting on Leela: 1 date to confirm

card.ask: Confirm Thursday: 8 am call, cold set, 5 hours.

chat.text: Brief and ten-shot list are out. Studio on hold for Thursday. Shot 4 is the slow pour over ice.
Thursday works. What time?
8 am. Ice shots first, before the lights warm the set.

os.title: Shoot, Thursday
rows: The 1 to 3 ratio in a glass

stages.line: Counted every kit part at HSR, saw caps at two weeks of cover, and placed PO-0071 for 6,000 on last order's terms.

chat.text: Caps are down to two weeks at 900 bottles a week. Placed PO-0071 for 6,000 on last order's terms.
And neck bands?
Five weeks. Bottles at three, cartons at four.

stages.line: Ran the upside-down test on batch C-02: 8 of 100 seals wept, limit 1%. Booked a Monday re-filter and re-cap.

running: Logging the seal test on C-02
Tracing weak seals to capping head 2
managing: Waiting on Meera: pass or reject C-02

card.ask: Batch C-02: 8 of 100 bottles weep at the seal. The limit is 1%.

chat.text: Upside-down test on C-02: 8 of 100 weep at the cap seal, limit 1%. 6 show sediment at the neck, limit 2%.
Rejecting it.
Re-filter and re-cap booked for Monday. Weak seals traced to capping head 2, logged for Farhan.

stages.line: Saw the bottle shipment slip three days, told Farhan, and moved the brew to Friday night so nothing else shifted.

running: Moving the brew to Friday, 10 pm
Sending the roastery the new slot

chat.text: Bottle shipment is three days behind. Lands Friday, not Tuesday.
Brew was set for Wednesday night.
Moved it to Friday, 10 pm. Bottles and concentrate meet Saturday. Nothing else moves.

stages.line: Got three quotes for 4,000 bottles, negotiated 30-day terms and free chipped-neck replacement, and drafted PO-0063 for ₹1,12,000.

managing: Waiting on Nikhil: 1 PO to approve

card.ask: Approve PO-0063: 4,000 amber bottles at ₹28, ₹1,12,000, paid in 30 days.

chat.text: Three quotes in for 4,000 amber bottles. Bengaluru is ₹4 more than Hosur but gives 30 days to pay, ships in 14, and replaces chipped necks.
Their round shoulder fits our filler.
PO-0063 drafted for ₹1,12,000. Sitting with Nikhil.

stages.line: Checked label proof v2 against 12 food labelling rules, caught the missing FSSAI number, and cleared v3 for print.

managing: Farhan: v2 back to the printer

chat.text: Proof v2 checked against the food labelling rules. One line missing: the FSSAI licence number.
Sending it back to the printer.
v3 is back with the FSSAI number, nothing else changed. Cleared for 4,000.

stages.line: Ran a blind tasting of five roasts, black and with milk, for seven tasters, and tallied the votes by 1:15 pm.

managing: Waiting on Nikhil: 1 roast to pick

card.ask: Pick the Hill Estate roast. Roast 4 won 5 of 7 votes.

chat.text: Blind tasting set: five roasts coded 1 to 5, black and with milk, seven tasters.
5 goes bitter with milk.
Tally: roast 4 scored 4.5 with milk, 4.2 black, 5 of 7 votes. Five tasters called roast 1 sour.

stages.line: Wrote the roaster role, screened 29 applicants down to four, and booked cuppings around everyone's calendars.

tap.what: made the offer to Anil M.

managing: Waiting on Varun: 1 offer to make

card.ask: Make the roaster offer. Anil M. scored 4.6 after cupping.

chat.text: Roaster role: 29 applicants in eight days. Four fit: specialty roasting, cold extraction, small batches.
Set cuppings for all four.
Done. Thursday and Friday at the roastery, around Nikhil's calendar. Scorecards are in the OS.

stages.line: Sat in on the 41-minute call, heard Nikhil say bottle it, and made it a project with an owner and three steps.

running: Taking notes in the product call
monitoring: Reviews asking for cold brew, daily

chat.text: That 1 am voice note. The estate coffee, steeped overnight. I want to bottle it.
As a concentrate, not ready-to-drink. Lasts longer, ships lighter.
Project opened: Hill Estate. Owner Nikhil. Step one, hire a roaster: Varun has it.

stages.line: 1:06 am, seven months before the doorstep. Everything that follows started with this.

running: Filing it under Ideas: Estate cold brew
Adding it to the next product review
managing: Holding it for Nikhil's product review

chat.text: Okay. Still up. That Chikmagalur estate lot, steeped overnight, beat everything we sell hot. Bottle it? Would people keep it in the fridge? Not sure. Look into it.
Saved to Ideas as Estate cold brew, with 23 chat requests for ready-to-drink attached. On the next product review.

end.line: Nikhil had the idea at 1:06 am. Seven months later it was on a doorstep. People tapped 8 times.
